phases.name: Foundation & Autonomous Control Plane
phases.summary: P0 establishes reproducible tooling, governance, schema validation, evidence contracts, atomic state, and fail-closed gates. No Linux feasibility claimed.

phases.name: Linux Platform Feasibility
phases.summary: P0F uses disposable probes to prove or explicitly limit global activation, text delivery, target identity, microphone/PipeWire capture, and Tauri packaging on Pop!_OS/COSMIC Wayland before architecture hardens (Ubuntu/GNOME is post-release, owner 2026-09-28).

phases.name: Core, IPC, Persistence & Privacy Baseline
phases.summary: P1 decides and implements session state machine, cancellation/timeouts, typed outcomes, daemon/client protocol, same-user IPC, crash journal, privacy-policy baseline, persistent store/migrations, daemon lifecycle, and deterministic mock path.

phases.name: Walking Skeleton
phases.summary: P2 delivers the first real plain but working path: trigger → microphone → real local ASR → final text → external target or Inbox fallback on the Pop!_OS COSMIC lane with cancellation, redacted logs, recoverable text, and CPU correctness.

phases.name: Desktop Client
phases.summary: P3 builds the Tauri/React client on the proven service path, with onboarding, diagnostics, accessible design system, and capability-driven UI that hides or labels post-1.0 features.

phases.name: Audio Reliability
phases.summary: P4 hardens capture, microphone lifecycle, PipeWire behavior, failure recovery, and only the proven 1.0 audio policies (leave + at least one crash-safe duck or pause).

phases.name: Production ASR, Model Manager & Compute Qualification
phases.summary: P5 chooses one reference local ASR engine/runtime for 1.0, provides CPU correctness fallback, qualifies model/runtime/driver/hardware tuples, and handles model download/cache/offline lifecycle with Vulkan/GPU pool and NPU where qualified.

phases.name: Integrated Dictation Beta
phases.summary: P6 turns the already-working product into a strong daily dictation beta and establishes measured latency/reliability baselines that later phases must preserve.

phases.name: Core Modes & Simple Personalization Only
phases.summary: P7 prioritizes Raw and Clean modes and simple profiles/settings not dependent on unreliable Wayland introspection; advanced profiles are capability-dependent or deferred.

phases.name: Privacy, History & Dictionary Essentials
phases.summary: P8 keeps only privacy/personalization essentials for a safe useful 1.0; advanced context, correction learning, project indexing, and fragile workflows are deferred unless proven low-risk.

phases.name: Reliability, Security, Accessibility & Performance Hardening
phases.summary: P9 attacks the working product with failure injection, security, accessibility, performance regressions, migration, lifecycle, resource exhaustion, and privacy leakage tests.

phases.name: Packaging & Reproducible Release Engineering
phases.summary: P10 produces the .deb (single Linux 1.0 installation artifact — owner decision 2026-08-22, no AppImage) with immutable builder baselines, dependency inventory, SBOM, notices, checksums, build identity, and provenance.

phases.name: Linux 1.0 Qualification & Release
phases.summary: P11 proves release artifacts (not dev builds) on the native Pop!_OS COSMIC reference environment (the only first-release lane, owner 2026-09-28) per bounded support and measured performance protocol.
